executive_summary: Today's cultural landscape is defined by the inescapable weight of legacy and transition, bridging the culinary rituals of the current season with profound loss in the entertainment world. As households embrace rapid summer-evoking meals highlighted in our newsletter coverage, the broader cultural conversation is abruptly anchored by the passing of beloved television icon Vincent Pastore. Known unforgettably as Salvatore 'Big Pussy' Bonpensiero on The Sopranos, Pastore's death at age eighty severs yet another vital link to the golden era of prestige television that forever changed modern storytelling. This intersection of daily life and retrospective mourning underscores how deeply audiences remain tethered to the enduring figures of our recent past even as daily routines march forward.

newsletters.title: Speedy dinners that sing of summer

items.headline: 1. Pork Tenderloin With Corn, Peaches and Lime
items.blurb: There’s a pork tenderloin in my freezer, and now I know how I’ll use it. Ali Slagle’s new skillet dinner was inspired by grilled lemongrass pork, drawing peaches, corn and cucumbers together with a punchy lime and fish sauce dressing. You can eat this one hot or at room temperature.

items.headline: 2. Dumpling Tomato Salad With Chile Crisp Vinaigrette
items.blurb: Hetty Lui McKinnon’s tomato dumpling salad is the stuff of summer dreams. It’s juicy, spicy, tangy and savory, and even initial doubters find they love it (one commenter called it the “skeptical-to-obsessed pipeline”). You can watch Hetty make it in the video on the recipe page.

items.headline: 3. Lemon-Garlic Grilled Chicken Breasts
items.blurb: Genevieve Ko has a step-by-step technique for cooking the best grilled chicken breasts, along with an extremely helpful video showing you how to do it (it’s easy, I swear). I think even the breast-avoidant cooks who watch that video will have to admit that these look really delicious.

items.headline: 4. Spicy Shrimp Masala
items.blurb: Zainab Shah brought this recipe to Cooking and described it as a “small miracle” — such is the speed with which you can make this fabulous dish and the fiery, layered depth of its flavors.

items.headline: 5. One-Pot Zucchini-Basil Pasta
items.blurb: I love pasta with zucchini, but the most delicious version of that calls for shredding the zucchini and then watching it shrink and caramelize in the pan — a process that can take more than 30 minutes (though it does make for a really excellent dinner). I can’t bring myself to do it after a day at work. So I was very happy when Alexa Weibel wrote this recipe, which is equally good in its own way, creamy, rife with pure zucchini flavor and remarkably fast to make.
